claim: The core acceptance criterion is not met: a formatted type `T` declared in a referenced assembly gets no formatter. The collector rejects any data type whose `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty. That is true for every type loaded from a metadata reference, which is the normal case when Project B references Project A's DLL. In that case MsgPack021 ('data type not supported') is reported and nothing is generated. The user's partial class is then left without `Serialize`/`Deserialize` and the build fails. The feature only works when `T` is declared in source in the same compilation, which is the opposite of the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterForReferencedAssemblyTypeTests.FormatterIsGeneratedForTypeFromMetadataReference. ProjectA is emitted to a PE image and referenced from ProjectB via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. Expect MsgPack021 among the generator diagnostics, plus CS0535 in the output compilation, so the test fails on head.

claim: The criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not implemented. Without a surrogate, `CreateContractlessMembers` always serializes every public read-write member by name as a string key and never reads attributes on `T`. Ignored attributes include `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`, `[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]`. A `T` with `[MessagePackObject]` + `[Key(0)]` therefore gets map-mode string keys instead of int keys, and members marked `[IgnoreMember]`, or left out of a `[DataContract]`, are serialized anyway. The SurrogateType path replaces this criterion rather than meeting it; ledger L18 says 'follow the requirement'.

On head the contractless member list includes Secret, so both fail. (generated tests: DataContractMembershipIsHonoured, MessagePackIgnoreMemberIsHonoured)

claim: The core requirement fails. `Collect` rejects any data type whose `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, and that is true for every type that comes from a referenced assembly (a metadata symbol). So for `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.MyType>`, where `ProjectA.MyType` lives in a referenced DLL, the generator reports MsgPack021 and emits no body. The partial class then fails to compile with CS0535. Only types declared in the same compilation work, which is exactly the case the feature was not needed for.

claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored when no SurrogateType is given. `CreateContractlessMembers` takes every public read-write member regardless of `[IgnoreMember]`, `[Key]` or `[MessagePackObject]`, and always uses string keys. Example: a T with `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key(0)] Id` and `[IgnoreMember] IgnoredSecret` gets a map-mode formatter that serializes IgnoredSecret. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured', and the wire format differs from T's own formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterReferencedAssemblyTests.FormatterHonoursIgnoreMemberOnFormattedType. On head the generated MyTypeFormatter source contains 'IgnoredSecret'.

claim: The contractless mode only emits public read-write members, so public get-only properties and readonly fields are skipped. ContractlessStandardResolver (the dynamic mode users have today) includes these members, which are serialized and restored through a constructor. A user switching to this attribute would get different wire content. Separately, a class with no parameterless constructor is rejected with MsgPack005 and gets no formatter at all.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a type with `public int A {get;set;}` and `public int B {get;}` (set in the constructor) using ContractlessStandardResolver, then using the generated formatter. Compare the bytes; the generated output will lack key B.

claim: Contractless mode sorts members by ordinal name, and it ignores any [DataContract]/[DataMember]/[MessagePackObject]/[Key] attributes on T. The requirement says T's own attributes must be honoured when present. The implementation honours only surrogate attributes, so a T with [Key] or [DataMember] gets contractless string keys. This differs from the dynamic resolver's output for the same T.

receipt_plan.detail: Take a T annotated with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] in a referenced assembly. Serialize it with the dynamic resolver, then with the [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter. The dynamic output is an array, while the generated output is a map with name keys.

claim: The attribute-based exclusion of user-declared formatters in the hand-written formatter scan runs per candidate class. Hand-written formatters that happen to be partial and annotated are now silently dropped from the generated resolver. Also, the diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are Error severity and are newly reported only for opted-in classes, so this should not affect existing users. However, Collect is called without an accessibility guard on the generated partial's own declared accessibility: the template emits `partial class` with no accessibility modifier. Combined with the user's `public partial class`, the generated formatter may be inaccessible if the formatter is nested, or its resolver registration may not compile in an internal resolver.

claim: Generated code for a user-declared formatter is emitted without regard to MessagePackSecurity. Serialization is generated but the contractless string-key path relies on the same generated deserializer that applies options.Security.DepthStep. This was not verified here and the diff does not show that the depth step is skipped, so no concrete issue is established. One checkable concern: a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class with a surrogate silently drops members (via IgnoreMember or unkeyed ones), which is not a security hole.
